verdict: Keep both on; they're a cheap safety net. Validation checks each value against the schema and records what fails. Coercion converts values to the schema's types, for example "$6.00" to 6.0. On RealKIE invoices, accuracy was the same with them on or off for every model, and they added up to 8% to the cost. Coercion changed no value, and validation flagged only Amazon Nova 2 Lite: 5 of 60 sections were missing a required field, which it records but doesn't fix.

validation_counts.note: Sections across all three runs. 'on' values: read from section metadata (metadata.validation, metadata.coercion). 'off' values: the same validate_extraction and coerce_extraction run offline over the stored output, to show what they would have done. Every validation failure was a required field (Advertiser) missing from Nova 2 Lite's output.
